question: Maya joined a running club because she wanted to improve her fitness. However, after injuring her ankle, she decided to take up swimming instead. Why did Maya choose swimming?
options: She wanted to compete in a swimming competition.
She needed an activity that put less pressure on her injured ankle.
The running club had closed.
Her doctor told her to stop all exercise.
correct: She needed an activity that put less pressure on her injured ankle.

question: Library Notice: 'Due to renovation work, the main library will be closed for two weeks. During this period, members may use the smaller branch on King Street.' Where can library members borrow books during the renovation?
options: At the main library entrance.
Only through the library website.
At the branch on King Street.
At the town hall.
correct: At the branch on King Street.

question: Dear Mr Adams, 'We regret to inform you that your order will arrive two days later than expected because of severe weather. We will refund your delivery charge. Thank you for your patience.' What will the company refund?
options: The full price of the order.
The delivery charge.
The cost of a replacement order.
The price of the most expensive item.
correct: The delivery charge.

question: Daniel normally takes the 8:00 bus to work. Because of roadworks, the bus company has announced delays of up to 20 minutes this week. Daniel must arrive at work by 9:00. What is the best thing for him to do?
options: Leave home earlier than usual.
Wait for the roadworks to finish before going to work.
Take the 8:30 bus instead.
Ask his manager to change his working hours without explaining why.
correct: Leave home earlier than usual.

question: A language school has cancelled its evening course because too few students enrolled. The school says that all students will receive a full refund within five working days. What will happen to the students?
options: They must pay for a different course.
They will receive their money back.
They can attend the course for free next year.
They must find more students to reopen the course.
correct: They will receive their money back.

question: Emma wrote: 'I wanted to buy a new laptop this month, but my washing machine suddenly broke. I used my savings to replace it, so I'll have to wait until next month to buy the laptop.' Why is Emma delaying her laptop purchase?
options: She no longer needs a laptop.
The laptop she wanted is unavailable.
She had to spend her savings on a washing machine.
She decided to save money for a holiday.
correct: She had to spend her savings on a washing machine.

question: Workplace Notice: 'Staff who wish to work from home on Fridays must request permission from their manager by Wednesday afternoon. Requests made after this deadline may not be approved.' When should an employee make the request?
options: On Friday morning.
By Wednesday afternoon.
After working from home.
At the end of the month.
correct: By Wednesday afternoon.

question: Leo planned to cycle to the countryside on Saturday, but the weather forecast predicts heavy rain. He has decided to visit a museum instead because it is indoors and easy to reach by train. Why has Leo changed his plans?
options: The museum is cheaper than cycling.
His bicycle needs repairing.
He wants to avoid being outdoors in bad weather.
The train service is unavailable.
correct: He wants to avoid being outdoors in bad weather.

question: Hotel Review: 'The room was small, but it was clean and quiet. The staff were helpful, and the breakfast was excellent. However, the hotel was quite far from the city centre, so we spent a lot of time travelling.' What was the main disadvantage of the hotel?
options: The breakfast was poor.
The room was noisy.
The staff were unhelpful.
Its location made travelling to the city centre inconvenient.
correct: Its location made travelling to the city centre inconvenient.

question: A manager emailed her team: 'Please send me your weekly reports by 3 p.m. Thursday. I need time to combine everyone's results before presenting them to the director on Friday morning.' Why does the manager need the reports by Thursday afternoon?
options: She wants to send the reports back to the employees.
She needs time to prepare a combined report for Friday.
The director will be unavailable on Thursday.
The team is having a meeting on Wednesday.
correct: She needs time to prepare a combined report for Friday.

question: A city notice says: 'From 1 November, residents can place food waste in the green bins provided. Plastic packaging must be placed in the blue recycling bins. Items left in the wrong bins may not be collected.' Where should residents put food waste?
options: In the green bins.
In the blue bins.
In any available bin.
Beside the bins.
correct: In the green bins.

question: Sami started a new job that pays more than his previous one. However, the commute takes an extra hour each day. He is thinking about moving closer to the office, but rents in that area are expensive. What is Sami trying to decide?
options: Whether he should quit working permanently.
Whether the company should reduce his salary.
How to balance his higher income against travel time and housing costs.
Whether to return to his previous job immediately.
correct: How to balance his higher income against travel time and housing costs.

question: Dear passengers, 'The 16:40 train to Oxford has been delayed by approximately 25 minutes because of a signalling problem. Passengers may use their tickets on the next available train without paying an additional fee.' What can affected passengers do?
options: Get a free taxi to Oxford.
Use their tickets on the next available train.
Travel only if they buy new tickets.
Request that the train return to its starting station.
correct: Use their tickets on the next available train.

question: Nadia used to study while listening to music because she thought it helped her concentrate. Recently, she noticed that she kept replaying songs and losing her place in her books. She now studies in silence. Why did Nadia change her habit?
options: She no longer likes music.
Her books became more difficult to buy.
Music was distracting her from studying.
Her teachers told her never to listen to music.
correct: Music was distracting her from studying.

question: A community centre offers free computer classes for adults on Tuesday and Thursday evenings. Participants must register online before attending. The centre provides computers, but students should bring their own headphones. What must a participant do before the first class?
options: Buy a computer.
Pay a course fee.
Bring a personal laptop.
Register online.
correct: Register online.

question: A customer writes: 'I ordered a blue jacket in size medium, but the parcel contained a black jacket in size small. I would like the correct item sent to me. I can return the incorrect jacket if you provide a prepaid label.' What does the customer want?
options: A refund for both jackets.
The correct jacket and a way to return the wrong one.
A larger black jacket.
A discount on a future order instead of a replacement.
correct: The correct jacket and a way to return the wrong one.

question: According to a health article, people who sleep too little may have difficulty concentrating during the day. The article recommends keeping a regular bedtime and avoiding caffeine late in the evening. What does the article suggest?
options: Drinking coffee before going to bed.
Changing sleep habits to improve daytime concentration.
Sleeping only when you feel tired.
Avoiding all drinks after lunch.
correct: Changing sleep habits to improve daytime concentration.

question: The school trip will cost €18 per student, including transport and museum entry. Students who want lunch provided must pay an additional €6. What is the total cost for a student who chooses the lunch option?

When Peter first moved to Germany, he found it difficult to make friends because he was shy about speaking German. He joined a local football team, where he met people who helped him practise the language. What helped Peter become more comfortable speaking German?
options: Avoiding conversations with other people.
Joining a local football team and meeting new people.
Studying grammar without speaking.
Moving to a different city immediately.
correct: Joining a local football team and meeting new people.

question: A job advertisement states: 'Applicants must have at least two years of customer service experience. Knowledge of a second language is an advantage but is not essential.' Which applicant meets the stated experience requirement?
options: Someone with one year of customer service experience and three languages.
Someone with two years of customer service experience who speaks only one language.
Someone with no customer service experience who speaks four languages.
Someone with six months of experience and a university degree.
correct: Someone with two years of customer service experience who speaks only one language.

question: The local council plans to introduce more cycle lanes to reduce traffic and air pollution. Some shop owners are concerned that fewer parking spaces will make it harder for customers to visit their businesses. What is the main disagreement about?
options: Whether cycling should be banned in the town.
Whether shops should close earlier.
How to improve the town while considering both environmental benefits and access to shops.
Whether public transport should be made free immediately.
correct: How to improve the town while considering both environmental benefits and access to shops.

question: A friend messages you: 'Sorry, I won't be able to meet you at 6. My meeting is taking longer than expected. Could we meet at 7 instead? If that's too late, we can choose another day.' What is your friend asking?
options: To cancel all future meetings.
To meet one hour later or arrange another day.
To meet earlier than planned.
To wait at the meeting room until midnight.
correct: To meet one hour later or arrange another day.

question: A university email says: 'Students who have not submitted their assignments should contact their tutors before Monday. Late submissions may receive a lower mark unless an extension has been approved.' What should a student do if they need more time?
options: Ignore the deadline.
Submit the same work twice.
Ask for an extension before submitting late.
Wait until the final mark is published.
correct: Ask for an extension before submitting late.

question: Olivia bought a second-hand bicycle online because it was cheaper than a new one. After a week, she discovered that the brakes needed replacing. The seller had mentioned that the bicycle was sold as seen, so she had to pay for the repair herself. What can we understand from this situation?
options: Second-hand products are always unreliable.
Olivia received a new bicycle instead.
The seller agreed to pay for the repair.
Buying a cheaper used item can sometimes lead to extra costs.
correct: Buying a cheaper used item can sometimes lead to extra costs.

question: A restaurant's website says: 'Tables can be reserved up to one month in advance. If you need to cancel, please notify us at least 24 hours before your booking.' When should a customer cancel to meet the stated policy?
options: One hour after arriving.
At least 24 hours before the booking.
Any time during the meal.
Only after receiving the bill.
correct: At least 24 hours before the booking.

question: A small company introduced flexible working hours. Employees can start between 7 a.m. and 10 a.m., but everyone must complete eight working hours and attend a team meeting at 10:30 a.m. What must all employees do?
options: Start work at exactly 7 a.m.
Work from home every day.
Complete eight hours and attend the 10:30 meeting.
Finish work before the team meeting.
correct: Complete eight hours and attend the 10:30 meeting.

question: A newspaper article explains that a town's new park has become popular with families because it includes a playground, walking paths, and shaded picnic areas. However, some residents say there are not enough rubbish bins, and litter is becoming a problem. What problem does the article highlight?
options: Families are not allowed to use the playground.
The park has too many walking paths.
The park is unpopular with residents.
The park needs more rubbish bins to help control litter.
correct: The park needs more rubbish bins to help control litter.

question: After several months of applying for jobs without success, Karim asked a former colleague to review his CV. She suggested making his achievements clearer and adapting the CV to each job. Karim followed her advice and received two interview invitations. What likely made the difference?
options: He stopped applying for jobs.
He improved how he presented his experience to employers.
He applied only for jobs that required no experience.
His former colleague applied for the jobs for him.
correct: He improved how he presented his experience to employers.

question: A travel website states: 'The city museum is free on the first Sunday of every month, but visitors must reserve a timed entry ticket online. On other days, tickets cost €12.' A visitor plans to go on the first Sunday. What must the visitor do to enter?
options: Pay €12 at the entrance.
Visit on a different day.
Reserve an entry time online.
Bring proof of living in the city.
correct: Reserve an entry time online.

question: A team leader says: 'Our project is behind schedule, so we need to focus on the most urgent tasks. Please postpone non-essential meetings and tell me immediately if you cannot meet a deadline.' What is the leader's main priority?
options: Holding more meetings to discuss every small detail.
Finishing the project by focusing on urgent work and identifying delays early.
Reducing communication among team members.
Starting a different project before completing this one.
correct: Finishing the project by focusing on urgent work and identifying delays early.
